messages:
sam: heads-up — saw a 2.3x p99 token latency spike across a handful of hosts at ~11:40 UTC. dashboards point at increased KV eviction activity during the burst.
anya: ugh. any repro or logs? which pool/host?
sam: pool=dedicated-europe-2, hosts: g-12,g-17,g-21. pasted top lines from runtime logs:
```
2026-03-15T11:40:12Z INFO kv: evict start batch=128 candidate=4096 policy=LRU free=64MB
2026-03-15T11:40:12Z WARN kv: reclaimed=48MB pages=12 reinserted=3 reuse_miss=7
2026-03-15T11:40:12Z INFO runtime: batch_dispatch latency_ms=12 queue_len=178
2026-03-15T11:40:12Z ERROR latency: tail_token_ms=184 eviction_pause_ms=42
```
anya: interesting — eviction_pause_ms 42 is small but spikes correlate. do you have profiler?
mason: i grabbed a short flamegraph during the window: https://perf.internal/runs/8492 (look at kv::evict -> pager::scan -> memcopy). shows unexpectedly long memcopy hotpath and work on reinserts.
kevin: could be fragmentation forcing many small copies. are we doing reinserts to head for FIFO vs LRU semantics? we changed reinsertion point in last deploy.
lia: reminder: change in kernel selection/batching a week ago also altered typical sequence lengths, so KV cache hit patterns shifted. increased long-context requests -> larger KV entries -> more page churn.
sam: repro steps I used: loadtest with long-context=32k tokens, concurrency=120, steady QPS=900, then 30s spike to 3k QPS. reproduces p99 jump reliably. minimal repro script:
```
./perf-run --model xlarge --seq 32768 --concurrency 120 --ramp 30 --burst 3000
```
kevin: can you attach kv telemetry dump from one host? need occupancy histogram, free fragments, avg-entry-size.
sam: attached short dump:
```
kv.occupancy_hist = [0: 1024, 1: 2048, 2: 4096, 3: 8192]
kv.free_fragments = 187
kv.avg_entry_bytes = 12.3k
kv.total_pages = 32768
kv.eviction_cycles = 128
```
lia: avg_entry_bytes=12.3k explains memcopy hit — we're moving ~12k chunks a lot. fragmentation 187 fragments is moderate but with large entries costs add up.
mason: i profiled and saw heavy syscalls during evict loop; our current eviction loop holds the page-lock while reinserting, which blocks dispatch. this could explain token tail latency.
anya: is this correctness bug (LRU vs FIFO) or just performance regression?
kevin: quick sanity: under pressure we saw some reinsert ordering anomalies earlier (ticket #ENG-7889) but we patched ordering correctness. current hypothesis: correctness ok, but reinserts + fragmentation + memcopy under heavy batch dispatch leads to GC-like stalls.
sam: i also saw a few WARN lines about 'reinsert dropped due to slot-dup' — might be a race-step we didn't fully close.
lia: can someone grep for 'slot-dup' occurrences across hosts and timeline?
mason: doing that now, searching logs from 11:30-11:50. will post counts.
pagerduty-bot: ALERT: KV_EVICT_LATENCY_HIGH on dedicated-europe-2 (met threshold). incident: INC-2026-0315.
kevin: short mitigation options: 1) temporarily lower max-batch-size to reduce concurrent memcopy pressure, 2) enable background async reinserts (decouple from eviction critical path), 3) increase reuse threshold so entries are less eagerly evicted.
anya: i'd prefer 2 but it's more code. 1 is fast and measurable. can we try a canary with batch_size=64 on one host?
sam: canary started on g-21 with batch_size=64 at 11:53. monitoring...
mason: initial numbers look promising: g-21 p99 down from 185ms -> 92ms within 1 minute of change. other hosts still high.
kevin: that supports memcopy pressure theory. but need long-term fix: async reinserts + avoid holding page-lock across memcopy.
lia: ops note: we'll also add more telemetry fields: reinserts_per_cycle, avg_reinsert_bytes, page_lock_hold_ms. add those to runtime before next rollout.
anya: assign owners? kevin for the async reinserts prototype, mason to add page_lock profiling, sam to run broader canary and log aggregation, lia to PR telemetry schema.
kevin: timeline: prototype in next 48h, perf test 72h, roll to canary.
sam: filed INC-2026-0315 and linked repro + logs. i'll post postmortem draft after we stabilize. thanks all. :thumbsup:
